claims.text: Tungsten-based refractory high-entropy alloys can be considered for high-temperature fusion-divertor applications.
A W-Ta-Cr-V alloy is an example of the proposed tungsten-containing refractory high-entropy-alloy system.
The initial alloy has a predominantly homogeneous, single-phase matrix.
Composition tailoring can promote SRO precipitate formation in a tungsten-rich matrix.
Heat treatment can promote SRO precipitate formation in a tungsten-rich matrix.
Fusion-divertor materials experience severe heat fluxes, particle fluxes, and radiation damage.
The presence and distribution of SRO precipitates constitute the structural mediator of the proposed thermal-conductivity change.
SRO precipitates scatter lattice phonons more effectively than a homogeneous tungsten matrix.
SRO precipitates introduce additional phonon-scattering centers.
The additional scattering centers decrease phonon mean free paths.
The additional scattering centers decrease phonon scattering times.
Reduced phonon mean free paths and scattering times lower the lattice component of thermal conductivity.
A tungsten-based alloy containing engineered SRO precipitates will have lower lattice thermal conductivity than an otherwise comparable homogeneous alloy.
The thermal-conductivity decrement and enhanced phonon scattering can be evaluated by thermal analysis and spectroscopy.
The magnitude of the effect depends on SRO precipitate size, distribution, and volume fraction.
Electronic heat conduction and operating temperature may mask changes in the lattice contribution.
The magnitude of the conductivity decrease depends on alloy composition.
